quick_skim.title: ActGaze: Learning Action-Grounded Gaze through Counterfactual Visual Interventions for High-Precision Manipulation
quick_skim.abstract: Current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models often struggle with high-precision robotic manipulation. We attribute this limitation primarily to their visual attention being dispersed across task-irrelevant regions. To address this issue, we propose ActGaze, a training approach that guides VLA policies to gaze on task-relevant regions, much like humans gaze on critical visual cues while executing precise movements. Unlike prior methods that rely on external labels for gaze supervision, ActGaze derives spatial supervision directly from the VLA's own action objective by using counterfactual visual interventions to identify regions that are critical for action prediction. Extensive real-robot experiments on four high-precision robotic manipulation tasks demonstrate that ActGaze induces more focused visual attention on task-relevant regions and consistently outperforms the base VLA policy and other visual-grounding approaches.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: VLA models struggle with precision because visual attention is dispersed. The paper proposes ActGaze, which derives gaze supervision from the action objective via counterfactual visual interventions, guiding policies to attend to task-relevant regions.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 视觉-语言-动作模型在精细操作中常表现不佳，作者认为主要原因是其视觉注意力分散在任务无关区域。该文提出ActGaze训练方法，引导策略像人类执行精确动作时那样注视任务相关区域，且不依赖外部注视标签，而是通过反事实视觉干预从动作预测目标中直接推导空间监督信号。在四项真实机器人高精度任务上的实验表明，该方法显著提升了操作成功率，说明以动作目标自监督生成注视是一种有效的注意力引导机制。
